claims.statement: The repository's stated validation norm is to prefer the narrowest quiet validation that proves the changed behavior and to preserve complete failure output.

GitHub Actions performs builds and signing only: build-test.yml (manual dispatch) drives a four-platform build matrix through build.yml with pnpm install but no cargo test or frontend test step, and pr-main-check.yml only validates the tauri.conf.json version format — so every test suite in the repo is run locally.

Rust unit tests are inline #[cfg(test)] modules inside the app crate (frontend/src-tauri, package `meetily`, the only workspace member with tests — llama-helper has none) and are run with cargo test from the repository root; they span audio/, summary/ (including summary_engine and templates), whisper_engine/, ollama/metadata.rs, onboarding.rs and analytics/.

The vad.rs suite pins: chunked and single-pass segmentation agree within ±1 segment; files larger than 960,000 samples (about 60 s at 16 kHz) process in 10-second chunks with monotonically increasing progress that must reach 100% and support callback cancellation (error mentions cancellation); ContinuousVadProcessor state persists across 10-second chunk boundaries; and 2000 ms redemption yields no more segments than 400 ms with segment durations staying at least 250 ms.

Batch VAD paths (audio import and retranscription) use VAD_REDEMPTION_TIME_MS = 2000 because whole-file processing would otherwise fragment speech at sentence gaps, while the live pipeline passes 400 ms on all platforms (both branches of the cfg! in pipeline.rs); a retranscription test asserts the 2000 ms constant.

The device_detection.rs tests pin InputDeviceKind classification (AirPods → Bluetooth, built-in names → Unknown, 3840 frames at 48 kHz → Bluetooth vs 512 frames → Wired, BlackHole → Wired), the adaptive timeout ranges (Wired 20–50 ms, Bluetooth 80–200 ms), and calculate_buffer_timeout clamping (80 ms base × 2 headroom ⇒ 160 ms).

The incremental_saver.rs tests pin the 30-second checkpoint contract: 60 seconds of 48 kHz audio produces exactly 2 checkpoints, finalize() merges checkpoints into one file and deletes .checkpoints/, and finalizing a recording with no checkpoints errors with "No audio checkpoints".

The summary/service.rs tests pin the title-stripping asymmetry (strip_title_if_present strips only a leading H1 — mid-document H1s, `#NoSpace`, and already-stripped input are preserved — while strip_leading_title returns an empty string when no `#` exists) and the English-cache extraction rules (a legacy `english_markdown` field is a cache miss; a matching source with a changed translation target reuses the cache; same-language regeneration and changed summary inputs reject it).

The summary/processor.rs tests pin the final-language action matrix (English target with non-English or unknown transcript normalizes to English; non-English target translates; failed normalization falls back to original markdown while cancellation is not swallowed) and the cached-English matrix; language_detection.rs tests pin weighted dominant-language detection with tie → None/Tie, short or unsupported text → None, and a guarantee that every mapped summary code has a language name.

Environment-dependent Rust tests are kept out of the default run: hardware tests are marked #[ignore] (Core Audio capture, system audio detector — run manually with --ignored) and platform smoke tests around permissions/system-audio commands print-and-continue when audio hardware is absent, so `cargo test` stays green on headless machines.

There is no `test` script in frontend/package.json and no JS test-runner configuration; the frontend tests are three standalone files under frontend/tests/lib run directly — the two bun:test files (blocknote-markdown.test.ts, summary-language-preferences.test.js) with bun, and onboarding-summary-model.test.mjs with plain node — and bun itself is not a declared repo dependency.

blocknote-markdown.test.ts pins blocksToMarkdownSafely: successful conversion returns { markdown, ok: true } and calls blocksToMarkdownLossy once; a thrown conversion returns the provided fallbackMarkdown with ok: false and logs console.error("Failed to convert BlockNote blocks to markdown", { source, blocksCount, error }); without a fallback, markdown is undefined.

summary-language-preferences.test.js mocks @tauri-apps/api/core and stubs window.localStorage to pin the folderless-meeting fallback contract: when the backend answers storage "local_fallback", the language persists under summaryLanguageFallback:<meetingId>, saving Auto (null) clears that key, detected languages cache under detectedSummaryLanguageFallback:<meetingId>, and a failing localStorage write rejects with "Failed to save summary language on this device".

onboarding-summary-model.test.mjs transpiles src/lib/onboarding-summary-model.ts with the typescript package and executes it in a node:vm context, asserting: an explicitly selected model wins over the recommendation; the recommended model becomes selected when nothing is selected; summaryModelDownloaded is true only when the selected model is ready (legacy Gemma availability must not make an undownloaded Qwen model ready); the size table (qwen3.5:2b = 1221 MB, qwen3.5:4b = 2614 MB, gemma3:1b = 1019 MB, unknown = 0) with ~GiB labels; and getDownloadTotalMb prefers a real total over the per-model estimate. Because it uses bare asserts, silence means pass.

The frontend local_fallback contract mirrors the Rust side: api_get_meeting_summary_language and api_save_meeting_summary_language return storage "local_fallback" (with language None) exactly when resolve_meeting_folder finds no non-empty folder_path for the meeting; otherwise the value is stored in the meeting folder's metadata.json and returned with storage "metadata".

scripts/inject_transcript.py seeds the platform-specific Meetily SQLite database from a CSV, creating meeting entries identical to those from normal recordings, so meeting/summary flows can be exercised without recording; it is the tool for DB-level validation and reports that the injected meeting should appear in the Meetily sidebar.

inject_transcript.py requires a CSV with a `text` column (one segment per non-empty value; missing column or zero segments is an error), estimates duration at 0.4 s per word with a 0.5 s minimum, assigns seg-<uuid4> ids and cumulative audio_start_time/audio_end_time, and inserts one `meetings` row (id `meeting-<uuid4>`, optional folder_path) plus one `transcripts` row per segment inside a single transaction that rolls back and exits non-zero on failure; afterwards it re-queries the meeting, segment count, and MAX(audio_end_time) and prints a verification summary.

inject_transcript.py resolves the database per platform (~/Library/Application Support/Meetily on macOS, %APPDATA%\Meetily on Windows with a Roaming fallback, ~/.config/Meetily on Linux), refuses to run if the file does not exist ("Make sure Meetily has been run at least once"), and accepts --db — pass a copy for scratch validation. The columns it writes (meetings.folder_path; transcripts.audio_start_time/audio_end_time/duration) are exactly those added by migration 20251006000000_add_audio_sync_fields.sql, so injected meetings support audio-transcript playback sync but contain no audio unless --folder-path points at a real folder.

main.rs unconditionally sets RUST_LOG=info before env_logger::init, so a shell-exported RUST_LOG (including the info|debug|trace selection exported by ./clean_run.sh) is overwritten before the logger reads it in the current code; the documented per-module recipe for debugging audio is RUST_LOG=app_lib::audio=debug, and console_utils::show_console likewise sets RUST_LOG=info when allocating a fresh Windows console.

perf_debug! and perf_trace! are defined in lib.rs to expand to log::debug!/log::trace! under #[cfg(debug_assertions)] and to nothing in release builds, and are re-exported crate-wide; the audio pipeline uses perf_debug! for its periodic summary gated to every 200 chunks or 60 seconds, and whisper_engine routes significant transcription-completion logging through perf_debug! and per-segment text through perf_trace! (only for audio longer than 30 s). Release builds therefore contain none of these lines, and plain log::debug! calls added directly are not eliminated.

audio/async_logger.rs provides a non-blocking AsyncLogger over an unbounded tokio mpsc channel with a 1000-message buffer flushed when full or every 100 ms and drop-tolerant sends so audio threads never block on log I/O; the async_debug!/async_info!/async_warn! macros lazily initialize a global logger only inside a tokio runtime context (main.rs notes it initializes lazily after the Tauri runtime starts). No module currently calls it, so it is ready-made infrastructure for new hot paths rather than an active log channel.

Instead of per-chunk logging, AudioPipeline::run feeds an AudioMetric (chunk id, sample count, duration ms, average level) into an AudioMetricsBatcher via the batch_audio_metric! macro; the batcher aggregates every 50 chunks or 5 seconds into an AudioMetricsSummary (total_chunks, total_samples, total_duration_ms, average_level, timespan, chunks_per_second) retrievable programmatically via get_summaries().

whisper_engine sets GGML_METAL_LOG_LEVEL=1 and WHISPER_LOG_LEVEL=1 at engine creation to suppress whisper.cpp/Metal C-library logs that bypass the Rust logging stack and would otherwise clutter output.

The in-app developer console is exposed as the show_console/hide_console/toggle_console Tauri commands — on Windows show_console allocates a console window and re-initializes env_logger at info, on macOS it opens Terminal running `log stream --process meetily --level info` (toggle detects that window via AppleScript) — and the ConsoleToggle React component drives them, hiding itself on non-Windows/macOS user agents.

AudioMixerRingBuffer mixes in fixed 600 ms windows (28,800 samples at 48 kHz; the adjacent "50 ms" comment is stale) with a per-side cap of 8× the window, logs a debug ring-buffer status every 200 add_samples calls, and on overflow drops the oldest samples after logging — a warn for the microphone side and an error for the system side ("SYSTEM AUDIO BUFFER OVERFLOW … THIS CAUSES DISTORTION!"); residual system-side overflow manifests as audible distortion in the saved recording rather than a crash, so these log lines are the definitive signal that the mixing stage lost audio.

Per-segment VAD observability: each accepted speech segment logs "📤 Sending VAD segment" at info while segments under 800 samples (50 ms at 16 kHz) log "⏭️ Dropping short VAD segment" at debug; batch import additionally logs "VAD detected N speech segments (redemption_time=2000ms)" plus average/min/max segment-duration statistics and the first 10 segments for inspection.

audio/diagnostics.rs exports log_device_capabilities, log_detection_summary, log_buffer_health (warns above 80% buffer utilization and flags Bluetooth-specific connection risk), log_mixer_status, and log_performance_summary as instrumentation helpers for debugging device detection, buffer health, and session performance.

Shutdown has a built-in chunk-loss verification loop: the transcription task counts queued and completed chunks with atomic counters and, after workers finish, retries the comparison up to 10 times (100 ms apart) before emitting the transcript-chunk-loss-detected event with the counts; stop_recording awaits the task with a 10-minute cap while emitting recording-shutdown-progress stages, then emits recording-stopped carrying folder_path and meeting_name — a queued/completed mismatch in the logs means chunks were lost between the pipeline and the workers.

Bluetooth playback distortion is a playback-side issue, not a recording bug: per BLUETOOTH_PLAYBACK_NOTICE.md, recordings are correct 48 kHz mono AAC files and macOS resampling to a headset's negotiated rate (8–44.1 kHz depending on profile/codec) shifts speed and pitch; verify with ffprobe (expect sample_rate=48000, channels=1, codec_name=aac) and re-test through speakers or wired headphones rather than changing the recording pipeline. playback_monitor::get_active_audio_output (per-platform name heuristics) feeds the BluetoothPlaybackWarning component, which polls every 5 seconds on playback screens and recommends wired playback.
